clips.send: Mohenjo-daro. today: Sindh, Pakistan. Perhaps 40,000 people — one of the biggest cities in the world 4,500 years ago. Streets laid out in a grid, covered brick drains, hundreds of wells and the “Great Bath”. Its writing (the Indus script, on small stone seals) has never been deciphered.

clips.send: Chang’an. today: Xi’an, China. Capital of the Western Han. Zhang Qian set out from here (138 BCE) — the start of the Silk Road.
clips.text: Chang’an. today: Xi’an, China. Capital of the Western Han. Zhang Qian set out from here (138 BCE) — the start of the Silk Road.

clips.send: Taxila. near Islamabad, Pakistan. A crossroads city: Persian province, visited by Alexander, governed by the young Ashoka. Famous for teachers and students; on the trade road to Central Asia.
clips.text: Taxila. near Islamabad, Pakistan. A crossroads city: Persian province, visited by Alexander, governed by the young Ashoka.. Famous for teachers and students; on the trade road to Central Asia.

clips.send: Sanchi. today: Madhya Pradesh, India. Ashoka began the Great Stupa here, a dome-shaped Buddhist monument holding relics. Its carved stone gateways were added about 2,000 years ago.
clips.text: Sanchi. today: Madhya Pradesh, India. Ashoka began the Great Stupa here, a dome-shaped Buddhist monument holding relics.. Its carved stone gateways were added about 2,000 years ago.

clips.send: Sarnath. near Varanasi, India. Where the Buddha gave his first teaching. Ashoka later put up a pillar here topped by four lions — today India’s national emblem.
clips.text: Sarnath. near Varanasi, India. Where the Buddha gave his first teaching.. Ashoka later put up a pillar here topped by four lions — today India’s national emblem.

clips.send: Bodh Gaya. today: Bihar, India. Here, says Buddhist tradition, Siddhartha Gautama sat under a tree and reached enlightenment, becoming the Buddha (“the awakened one”).
clips.text: Bodh Gaya. today: Bihar, India. Here, says Buddhist tradition, Siddhartha Gautama sat under a tree and reached enlightenment, becoming the Buddha (“the awakened one”).

clips.send: Susa. today: Shush, Iran. An administrative capital of the Persian kings and the east end of the Royal Road.
clips.text: Susa. today: Shush, Iran. An administrative capital of the Persian kings and the east end of the Royal Road.

clips.send: Harappa. today: Punjab, Pakistan. The first Indus city dug up by archaeologists (1920s) — so the whole culture is also called “Harappan”. Large granaries, brick houses and wells; perhaps 23,000+ people at its height.
clips.text: Harappa. today: Punjab, Pakistan. The first Indus city dug up by archaeologists (1920s) — so the whole culture is also called “Harappan”.. Large granaries, brick houses and wells; perhaps 23,000+ people at its height.

clips.send: Dont mix up: Buddhism began in India but later became much smaller there; it spread to Sri Lanka, Southeast Asia, China, Korea and Japan.
clips.text: Dont mix up: Buddhism began in India but later became much smaller there; it spread to Sri Lanka, Southeast Asia, China, Korea and Japan.

clips.send: India and Persia sat between the Mediterranean and China. Goods, armies, religions and number systems all passed through.
clips.text: India and Persia sat between the Mediterranean and China. Goods, armies, religions and number systems all passed through.

clips.send: Babylon. near Hillah, Iraq. Cyrus took Babylon in 539 BCE and recorded it on the Cyrus Cylinder. Alexander the Great died here in 323 BCE.
clips.text: Babylon. near Hillah, Iraq. Cyrus took Babylon in 539 BCE and recorded it on the Cyrus Cylinder.. Alexander the Great died here in 323 BCE.

clips.send: Persepolis. near Shiraz, Iran. Darius I began this ceremonial capital around 518 BCE. Stone reliefs show people from all over the empire bringing gifts to the king. Alexander’s army burned it in 330 BCE; the ruins still stand.

clips.send: Pataliputra. today: Patna, India. Capital of the Mauryan Empire — a Greek visitor, Megasthenes, described its long wooden walls. Later a capital of the Gupta kings too.
clips.text: Pataliputra. today: Patna, India. Capital of the Mauryan Empire — a Greek visitor, Megasthenes, described its long wooden walls.. Later a capital of the Gupta kings too.

clips.send: Kalinga (Dhauli). today: Odisha, India. Ashoka conquered Kalinga in about 261 BCE. In his own words, the suffering of the war filled him with deep regret. At Dhauli, near the battlefield, his edicts are still carved into a rock.

clips.send: Lothal. today: Gujarat, India. A trading port with a large brick basin that many archaeologists think was a dockyard. Beads, cotton and seals from Indus cities reached Mesopotamia by sea.

clips.send: 印度和波斯位于地中海世界和中国之间，商品、军队、宗教和数字都从这里经过。

clips.send: 桑奇。今印度中央邦。阿育王在这里开始修建大佛塔（窣堵坡）——一座存放佛舍利的圆顶建筑。雕刻精美的石门大约是2000年前加上去的。

clips.send: 摩亨佐·达罗。今巴基斯坦信德省。可能有4万人，是4500年前世界上最大的城市之一。街道呈棋盘状，有砖砌的带盖下水道、数百口水井和“大浴池”。刻在小石印章上的印度河文字至今没有被破译。

clips.send: 菩提伽耶。今印度比哈尔邦。据佛教传说，乔达摩·悉达多在这里的一棵菩提树下悟道成佛（“佛陀”意为“觉悟者”）。

clips.send: 巴比伦。今伊拉克希拉附近。公元前539年居鲁士攻占巴比伦，并把这件事刻在“居鲁士圆柱”上。公元前323年亚历山大死于这里。

clips.send: 哈拉帕。今巴基斯坦旁遮普。考古学家在20世纪20年代最早发掘的印度河城市，所以这个文明也叫“哈拉帕文明”。有大型粮仓、砖房和水井，鼎盛时可能有两万多人。

clips.send: 长安。今西安。西汉都城。张骞从这里出发出使西域（公元前138年），这里是丝绸之路的起点。

clips.send: 波斯波利斯。今伊朗设拉子附近。大流士一世约公元前518年开始修建这座礼仪性都城。石浮雕上刻着帝国各地的人向国王献礼。公元前330年亚历山大的军队焚毁了它，遗址至今犹存。

clips.send: 鹿野苑（萨尔纳特）。今印度瓦拉纳西附近。佛陀第一次说法的地方。后来阿育王在这里立起一根顶上有四只狮子的石柱——今天它是印度的国徽。

clips.send: 塔克西拉（呾叉始罗）。今巴基斯坦伊斯兰堡附近。一座十字路口城市：做过波斯的行省，亚历山大到过这里，年轻的阿育王在这里当过总督。以学者和学生众多闻名，位于通往中亚的商路上。

clips.send: 羯陵伽（道利）。今印度奥里萨邦。约公元前261年阿育王征服羯陵伽。按他自己的诏书所说，战争带来的苦难让他深深懊悔。在古战场附近的道利，岩石上至今还刻着他的诏书。

clips.send: 华氏城。今印度巴特那。孔雀王朝的都城，希腊使节麦加斯梯尼曾描述过它长长的木城墙。后来也是笈多王朝的都城。

clips.send: 易错点：古印度河流域文明（哈拉帕、摩亨佐·达罗，今天大多在巴基斯坦）早在约公元前1900年后就衰落了；种姓制度是后来雅利安人进入印度后形成的，佛教也是在恒河流域创立的。另外，“波斯”就是今天的伊朗。

clips.send: 洛塔尔。今印度古吉拉特邦。一座贸易港口，有一个巨大的砖砌水池，很多考古学家认为它是船坞。印度河城市的珠子、棉布和印章经海路运到了两河流域。
